On Thu, May 20, 2027 at 9:14 AM Alyssa Chen <alyssa@brightcart.com> wrote:
> We're seeing a sudden spike in p99 latency for Redwood API calls from BrightCart's checkout flow starting ~08:50 PDT.

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Observed correlation between p99 spikes and a sharp drop in KV cache global hit-rate for the tenant. Hit-rate went from ~87% down to ~22% across the period.
- We can see multiple concurrent KV miss bursts targeted at a small set of shards (hot shards). The worker queues show HOL blocking where large batches wait on a single shard to respond.
- There are a few long-tail requests (>1.5s) that align with retry/backoff cascades creating queuing amplification.

Likely proximate cause: a recent config drift rolled out (auto-evict-policy=aggressive, kv_slot_count reduced for the tenant) that appears to have reduced effective local cache entries and increased remote KV lookups. Combined with our continuous-batching behavior this causes lots of small KV misses coalescing into big batches that lock the hot shard.

Immediate mitigations I recommend now (low risk):
1) Set per-tenant max_batch_size=8 for the BrightCart routes (currently 64) to reduce HOL lock windows.
2) Temporarily pin the tenant's kv_shard_affinity to 8 to spread keys away from the hot shard.
3) Re-enable local prefix caching for the checkout route (it looks like that flag was disabled).

I'll push stats snippet in a sec.

- Marissa
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Looping in a short technical summary for execs and product to approve the mitigations:

Summary: root cause appears to be a config drift that reduced per-tenant KV slot allocations and enabled an aggressive eviction policy. The runtime's continuous batching behavior magnified the impact by queuing multiple requests behind locks on a small set of hot shards — classic HOL (head-of-line) blocking.

Impact: elevated p99 and 5xx during the window; checkout conversions impacted for ~35 mins (visible revenue impact).

Proposed plan (approved by SRE):
- Immediate (within 15m): apply per-route max_batch_size=8 and re-enable prefix caching (no restart) — this is reversible and low-risk.
- Short term (30–90m): pin kv_shard_affinity to spread hot keys, apply eviction-policy=conservative. This is a config flip; we can do it without a full cluster restart but it will cause localized cache re-population traffic. Expect transient tail latency ~200–400ms for affected keys for ~10 min.
- Fallback (if latency not improved): rolling restart of 10% of the serving pool to clear pathological kernel state; estimated service disruption: <1% requests retried for <30s per cell.

Estimated cost & approvals: pinning shards and conservative eviction increases memory usage by ~8% (BrightCart cost estimate ~$1200/day for the extra reserved). Rolling restarts are ops time only.

I'll implement the immediate mitigations now (ETA 10m) and monitor.

-Vivek

Subject: Action plan and follow-up: BrightCart checkout p99 & 5xx incident (May 20)

Mark / Alyssa — thank you for your patience as we investigated.

What we did:
- Applied immediate mitigation (max_batch_size=8, prefix caching re-enabled) at 10:27 PDT on 20 May. Observed p99 drop from 2400ms -> ~520ms within 8 minutes.
- Pinned kv_shard_affinity and switched eviction-policy to conservative at 11:05 PDT; cache warmed over ~12 minutes.
- Monitored for 48 hours. No recurrence in that time window.

Why it happened: a config drift reduced per-tenant KV slots and enabled an aggressive eviction policy during a routine autoscaler test. That change, combined with continuous batching, allowed hot shards to become congested leading to HOL blocking and retry amplification.

Next steps / ask:
- We recommend keeping the conservative eviction policy and increased slot allocation for BrightCart for the next 30 days while we run a tail-latency calibration job.
- If BrightCart approves, we can enable a soft reserve (extra memory) for hot-prefixes — this adds estimated cost of $1200/day and requires exec sign-off.
- I'll schedule a 30-minute post-incident review (PIR) with BrightCart and our runtime team (link: https://meet.google.com/xyz-abc-123).

Attachments: runbook_patch.diff (contains the small config changes we applied and rollback steps).

Please let me know if you'd like an immediate call — otherwise I'll plan the PIR for next week and share the final RCA.
